mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen sharply from -43.4 at t-1w to -24.4 at t-0w, indicating a rebound in discretionary shopping and recreation activity that should persist as households resume pre-restriction routines over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -43.4 to -24.4 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the recent two-week rebound.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility rises above -25 for two consecutive weeks, it signals relaxed commuting restrictions that will drive adjacent weekday retail traffic upward, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -33.7 to -30.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 14 days even after WORKPLACES crosses above -25 for two consecutive weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL and TRANSIT both move favorably in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, co-movement of PARKS and WORKPLACES toward less-negative values reflects loosened public-health restrictions on outdoor and commercial venues, which jointly sustains a four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC as restriction relief compounds.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -40.4 to -34.0 and WORKPLACES improved from -33.7 to -30.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC trend reverses downward over the next 28 days despite continued improvement in both PARKS and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: With the decision point in mid-June, seasonal lengthening of daylight and warmer weather typically increases outdoor and retail-adjacent activity independent of policy, so PARKS mobility recovery is a seasonal leading indicator of sustained RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -43.0 at t-2w to -34.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to trend upward over the next 28 days despite continued seasonal PARKS improvement through June.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT mobility rises above -60 week-over-week, it indicates a critical mass of commuters and shoppers returning to public transit, which within one week translates into a visible short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC as transit-dependent shoppers resume trips.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -72.7 to -64.7, approaching the -60 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within the following week after TRANSIT crosses above -60.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained near baseline (-3.6 to 0.4) while RETAIL_REC lags far below baseline; as the gap between essential and discretionary mobility narrows, pent-up discretionary demand is released, interacting to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC widens or stays constant over the next 28 days instead of narrowing via RETAIL_REC growth.
